summary: `coverage` is a hand-authored top-level command registered through the novel hook. It exists because absorb manifest rows 2 and 3 were approved against the command path `nepra-pp-cli coverage`, which resolved to nothing, so the Phase 3 completion gate failed on both. It joins the CLI's three in-code catalogues into one ledger and makes NO request.
reason: Row 2's parity target was ebillpakistan.pk's NEPRA_SOURCE object, a hand-maintained JavaScript literal recording where each tariff figure came from; row 3's was its scripts/tariff-staleness.mjs, which exits 1 past STALE_AFTER_DAYS=90 for ONE surface. Beating both needs machine-checkable provenance per artifact and a staleness signal over EVERY surface. Three constraints shaped the result. (1) THE JOIN KEY IS THE PATH, NEVER THE ID: verify and sources BOTH name the FY2023-24 workbook "gen-2023-24" while carrying different byte floors (verify's measured 493,187 against sources' blanket 400,000), so an id join fuses two different claims and silently drops one. Joining on the request path keeps both and records floor_owner; the seven generation workbooks produce seven recorded disagreements rather than seven silent overwrites. (2) http_status IS NEVER RECORDED ON A SUCCESS. The generated client's Get/GetWithHeaders/GetNoCache all return (json.RawMessage, error) and discard the status int, so recording "200" would assert a value never observed; a non-2xx that WAS observed is carried per row as http_status_as_of. (3) ONLY sha256_content IS COMPARABLE ACROSS FETCHES. Cloudflare's email-obfuscation filter rewrites every data-cfemail token per response, so two identical fetches of one page seconds apart returned the same 74,431 bytes with DIFFERENT sha256_raw values; the same page is also 74,431 vs 74,792 bytes depending on the request's Accept header, and every text/html body on this host carries a ~361-byte injected RUM beacon. A staleness or drift gate over raw bytes would therefore report drift on every run for a page that has not changed.
reapply_after_regen: Both files are markerless and hand-authored, and the command registers itself from init() through registerNovelCommand, so nothing in generated root.go needs editing and a regen cannot drop the wiring. The command reads verifySurfaces, sourcesDocs() and eventSurfaces directly, so it compiles or fails loudly if any of those change shape. VERIFY WITH DATA, NOT A GREP: `coverage --json` must report 83 surfaces and 7 floor_disagreements, and `coverage --check-stale --stale-after 0` must exit 6 while `coverage --stale-after 0` alone exits 0 — that split is the whole measurement-versus-gate contract.
validated_outcome: 83 surfaces joined from sources (63), verify (11) and events (28), with the three pairwise overlaps reproducing an independent set-union exactly: sources INTERSECT verify = 8 paths, sources INTERSECT events = 11 (the DISCO tariff pages), events INTERSECT verify = 0. All 83 rows resolve to a serving command. 7 floor disagreements recorded, one per generation workbook. Makes no request, proven with HTTP(S)_PROXY pointed at 127.0.0.1:1. Exit codes: 0 the ledger printed, 2 a usage refusal (unknown --kind, negative --stale-after, a positional argument), 6 --check-stale found a surface past the window. Under --check-stale the gate message goes to stderr and stdout stays valid JSON. MUTATION-VERIFIED 8/8: joining on the id, letting sources' floor win, swallowing the disagreements, treating an unaged surface as fresh, a >= boundary off-by-one, fabricating a 200 status, dropping the omission declaration, and an unrecognised kind serving nothing are each killed by a test.
